notes: Switching to Protease Inhibitor-Sparing Regimen for Cardiovascular Disease. Virologically suppressed HIV. PI-sparing improved lipids, reduced CV events (6.2% vs 9.6%). Regimen choice matters for CV risk.
Treatment-naive HIV. Raltegravir vs PIs. Better lipid profile with raltegravir. Fewer CV events long-term (3% vs 4.7%). Integrase inhibitors more CV-friendly than PIs.

Abacavir SUbstitution in paTiEnts at Risk for cardiovascular disease. Abacavir increased endothelial dysfunction, inflammatory markers. More CV events (6.2% vs 3.1%). Abacavir concerns for high CV risk patients.
Randomized Trial to Prevent Vascular Events in HIV. Low-moderate CV risk on ART. STOPPED EARLY. Statins reduced MACE 35% (HR 0.65, p=0.002). BREAKTHROUGH: proved statins beneficial in HIV. NEJM 2023.
Strategic Timing of AntiRetroviral Treatment. Early ART reduced AIDS + serious non-AIDS (including CV) events 72% (HR 0.28, p<0.001). Early treatment better for all outcomes.
Strategies for Management of AntiRetroviral Therapy. STOPPED EARLY. Episodic therapy INCREASED CV disease 60% (HR 1.6, p=0.05). Continuous ART critical. Treatment interruptions harmful.
South African trial. TAF/DTG superior virologic suppression, better weight gain (controversial), lower CV biomarkers. Modern regimens likely safer CV profile.
